places.name: Dublin
places.summary: Ireland's capital straddles the River Liffey, with Georgian squares, Trinity College, big free national museums and a famous pub and music scene. Compact enough to explore on foot and the main arrival point for most trips.
facts: Driving and parking in the centre are slow and expensive; use the Luas tram, buses or walk
Leap Visitor Card covers buses, Luas and DART at a discount
Many of the national museums and galleries are free
Hotels are pricey; book well ahead for weekends and events
places.season: Mild and often damp all year; long light evenings in June, short days in December.

places.name: Trinity College & the Book of Kells
places.summary: The 9th-century illuminated gospel book is displayed at Trinity College, followed by the soaring Long Room of the Old Library. The campus itself, founded in 1592, is a calm green oasis in the city centre.
facts: Timed tickets (~€20–25) online; slots sell out in summer
Go at the first slot of the day to avoid the crush in the treasury
The Long Room is undergoing a multi-year conservation project, so some books may be removed

places.name: Dublin Castle
places.summary: Seat of British rule in Ireland for 700 years, now a mix of Georgian State Apartments, a medieval tower and Viking-era excavations. The free Chester Beatty Library in the grounds is one of the city's best small museums.
facts: Self-guided State Apartments ~€8; guided tour (includes the undercroft) costs a little more
State rooms can close at short notice for official events
Combine with the free Chester Beatty Library next door

places.name: Christ Church Cathedral
places.summary: Dublin's oldest cathedral, founded by the Norse around 1030 and rebuilt by the Normans, with a vast medieval crypt. Linked by a bridge to Dublinia, a family-friendly Viking and medieval museum.
facts: Entry ~€10; combined tickets with Dublinia available
Crypt holds the famous mummified cat and rat
A 10-minute walk from St Patrick's Cathedral

places.name: St Patrick's Cathedral
places.summary: Ireland's largest church, a 13th-century Gothic cathedral where Jonathan Swift was dean and is buried. The adjoining park is a pleasant stop.
facts: Entry ~€10; check the website for service times when visiting is limited
Choral evensong is free and open to all
Allow about 45 minutes

places.name: National Museum of Ireland – Archaeology
places.summary: Ireland's treasury of prehistoric gold, the Ardagh Chalice, Tara Brooch and the eerie Iron Age bog bodies. A free, world-class collection in a grand Victorian building on Kildare Street.
facts: Free entry
The bog bodies in 'Kingship and Sacrifice' are the standout
Opens later on Sundays and Mondays; check before going

places.name: National Gallery of Ireland
places.summary: Free national art collection with old masters including Caravaggio's 'Taking of Christ', and a strong Irish room featuring Jack B. Yeats. A good rainy-day stop by Merrion Square.
facts: Free entry (some temporary exhibitions charge)
Merrion Square's Georgian doors and the Oscar Wilde statue are next door
Café on site

places.name: Guinness Storehouse
places.summary: Seven-floor visitor experience in a former fermentation building at St James's Gate brewery, ending with a pint in the rooftop Gravity Bar. Touristy but Ireland's most visited attraction, with great city views.
facts: Tickets ~€26+ and cheaper online for off-peak slots; book ahead
Pint or soft drink included
20-minute walk from Temple Bar, or take a bus/Luas to James's

places.name: Kilmainham Gaol
places.summary: Former prison where leaders of the 1916 Easter Rising were executed, now visited on moving guided tours that tell the story of Irish independence. One of the most powerful sights in Dublin.
facts: Guided tour only (~€8); book online well ahead as it sells out days in advance
Tour lasts about 1 hour plus the museum
Combine with the Irish Museum of Modern Art next door

places.name: EPIC The Irish Emigration Museum
places.summary: Interactive museum in the CHQ building on the Docklands telling the story of the 10 million people who left Ireland and their impact abroad. Modern, well-designed and good for families.
facts: Tickets ~€20+; online booking advised in summer
The Jeanie Johnston famine ship replica is moored nearby
Allow 1.5 hours

places.name: Temple Bar
places.summary: Cobbled cultural quarter between Dame Street and the Liffey, packed with pubs, live music, galleries and the Saturday food market. Busy and pricey, but lively at night.
facts: Pints here are noticeably dearer than elsewhere in the city
Ha'penny Bridge is right next to it
Can get rowdy late at weekends

places.name: Phoenix Park
places.summary: One of Europe's largest enclosed city parks, home to a herd of wild fallow deer, Dublin Zoo and Áras an Uachtaráin, the President's residence. Good for a walk or bike ride away from the traffic.
facts: Free; bikes can be rented at the Parkgate Street entrance
Deer are usually around the Fifteen Acres; don't feed them
Free tours of Áras an Uachtaráin on Saturdays from the visitor centre

places.name: St Stephen's Green & Grafton Street
places.summary: Victorian city-centre park with a lake, bridges and statues, at the top of pedestrianised Grafton Street with its buskers and shops. A natural pause between Trinity and the Georgian quarter.
facts: Free; gates close around dusk
The Little Museum of Dublin is on the north side of the Green
Grafton Street buskers are best on weekend afternoons

places.name: Glasnevin Cemetery
places.summary: Ireland's national cemetery, resting place of Daniel O'Connell, Michael Collins and Charles Stewart Parnell, with a good museum and guided tours. The adjoining National Botanic Gardens are free.
facts: Grounds free; museum and guided tours ticketed (~€15)
Tours explain the history of independence through its graves
Combine with the free National Botanic Gardens next door

places.name: Howth
places.summary: Fishing village on a headland north of the city, with seafood restaurants on the pier, seals in the harbour and a ruined abbey. An easy half-day escape by DART train.
facts: DART from the city centre takes about 30 minutes
Weekend market by the station
Gets crowded on sunny weekends

places.name: Howth Cliff Path Loop
places.summary: Waymarked loop around Howth Head with sea cliffs, heather and views over Dublin Bay to the Baily Lighthouse and the Wicklow Mountains. One of the best coastal walks within reach of a capital city.
facts: Free; start from Howth DART station or the Summit car park
Several colour-coded loops from 6 km to 12 km
Paths are narrow and close to the cliff edge in places
places.caution: Keep to the path; the cliff edges are unfenced and dangerous in wind.

places.name: Malahide Castle & Gardens
places.summary: Castle home of the Talbot family for almost 800 years, set in parkland with a walled botanic garden and butterfly house. Combine with the seaside village of Malahide.
facts: Castle tour and gardens ~€15; gardens-only ticket cheaper
DART to Malahide takes about 25 minutes from Connolly
Park grounds are free

places.name: Wicklow Town
places.summary: County town on the coast with a harbour, a ruined Black Castle on the headland and the restored Wicklow Gaol. A practical base for Glendalough and the Wicklow coast, under an hour from Dublin.
facts: Free parking along the harbour and Murrough
Black Castle headland walk takes 20 minutes
Limited accommodation; book ahead in summer

places.name: Drogheda
places.summary: Historic town on the River Boyne with medieval St Laurence's Gate and the shrine of St Oliver Plunkett's head in St Peter's Church. The best base for Brú na Bóinne and the Boyne Valley.
facts: Millmount Fort and museum overlook the town
Train from Dublin Connolly takes about 40–60 minutes
Newgrange visitor centre is 15 minutes' drive

places.name: Glendalough
places.summary: Early medieval monastic city founded by St Kevin in a glacial valley with two lakes, a 30 m round tower and stone churches. Woodland trails lead to the Upper Lake in Wicklow Mountains National Park.
facts: Site free; visitor centre ~€5
Car parks (paid, ~€4) fill by late morning on weekends; arrive early
Lower Lake to Upper Lake walk is about 30 minutes on the Green Road
places.season: Lovely in autumn colour; weekends in summer are very busy.

places.name: Spinc & Glenealo Valley Walk
places.summary: Waymarked loop (white arrows) up a boardwalk staircase to the cliff edge above the Upper Lake, round the Glenealo valley past old miners' village ruins. The best views of Glendalough.
facts: About 9 km, 3–4 hours; steep steps at the start
Start at the Upper Lake car park (paid) or walk from the visitor centre
Boots and waterproofs advised
places.caution: Weather changes quickly on the open hillside; carry a jacket.

places.name: Powerscourt Estate & Gardens
places.summary: Palladian house with some of Europe's finest formal gardens: Italian terraces, Japanese garden and a lake framed by the Sugar Loaf mountain. Close to Enniskerry, 40 minutes from Dublin.
facts: Gardens ~€13 (house interior is mostly shops and café)
Allow 2 hours for the full garden loop
Free parking on site

places.name: Powerscourt Waterfall
places.summary: At 121 m, Ireland's highest waterfall, tumbling down a rock face into a parkland valley on the Powerscourt Estate. Picnic spot with giant sequoias.
facts: Separate ticket (~€7) and access road from the gardens, 6 km away
Best after rain; can be a trickle in dry summers
Closes earlier in winter

places.name: Lough Tay (Guinness Lake) & Sally Gap
places.summary: Dark peaty lake with a white sand beach below the road to Sally Gap, on the estate of the Guinness family. The bleak blanket bog of the Military Road around it is classic Wicklow upland scenery.
facts: Roadside parking at the viewpoint on the R759
The lake shore is private land; view from the road
Combine with the Military Road drive to Glendalough
places.caution: Road is narrow and can be closed by snow or ice in winter.

places.name: Russborough House
places.summary: Grand 18th-century Palladian mansion by the Blessington Lakes, famous for its art collection and several notorious art thefts. Parkland walks, a maze and a birds of prey centre.
facts: House by guided tour (~€15); grounds cheaper
Near the Wicklow Gap road from Glendalough
Café on site

places.name: Wicklow Gaol
places.summary: Grim 18th-century prison turned interactive museum, with costumed guides telling stories of rebels, famine prisoners and transportation to Australia.
facts: Tickets ~€10, guided tours run regularly
Reputed to be haunted; night tours sometimes run
Allow about an hour

places.name: Avoca
places.summary: Small village in the Vale of Avoca, home to Ireland's oldest working hand-weaving mill and known as the setting of the TV series 'Ballykissangel'.
facts: Free to visit the weaving mill and shop
Meeting of the Waters beauty spot is a few km north
Easy stop between Wicklow and Wexford

places.name: Brittas Bay
places.summary: Five km of white sand backed by dunes, one of the most popular beaches on the east coast. Gentle bathing water and lifeguards in summer.
facts: Paid car parks in summer
Very busy on hot weekends
Dunes are a protected habitat; stay on paths

places.name: Bray to Greystones Cliff Walk
places.summary: Seven-km coastal path around Bray Head between two DART stations, with sea cliffs and views back to Dublin Bay. Finish with lunch in Greystones and take the train back.
facts: Free; about 2 hours one way
DART connects both ends to Dublin
Sections may close after rockfalls; check before you go
places.caution: Sections of the path have been closed by landslides; obey closure signs.

places.name: Brú na Bóinne (Newgrange & Knowth)
places.summary: UNESCO-listed Neolithic passage tombs older than the pyramids: Newgrange, with its winter-solstice roof box, and Knowth, with Europe's largest collection of megalithic art. Visited only by shuttle bus tours from the visitor centre.
facts: All visits start at the visitor centre south of the river; you cannot drive to the tombs
Tour tickets ~€10–20 depending on tombs; book online, summer slots sell out
Allow 3 hours for both tombs; Knowth is usually closed in winter

places.name: Slane & Hill of Slane
places.summary: Georgian estate village on the Boyne, overlooked by the hill where St Patrick is said to have lit his Easter fire. Slane Castle hosts big concerts and a whiskey distillery.
facts: Hill of Slane ruins free and open access
Slane Distillery tours need booking
Close to Brú na Bóinne

places.name: Monasterboice
places.summary: Early Christian monastic site with a round tower and Muiredach's High Cross, the finest carved high cross in Ireland. Free and atmospheric, just off the M1.
facts: Free, open access
Small car park; quiet early or late
Combine with Mellifont Abbey nearby

places.name: Old Mellifont Abbey
places.summary: Ruins of Ireland's first Cistercian abbey, founded in 1142, with an unusual octagonal lavabo. Peaceful riverside setting.
facts: Grounds free; visitor centre open in summer only
Allow 30–45 minutes
10 minutes from Drogheda

places.name: Hill of Tara
places.summary: Ancient ceremonial seat of the High Kings of Ireland, with grassy earthworks, the Stone of Destiny and wide views over Meath. More about atmosphere than visible ruins.
facts: Free open access; guided tours in summer
Wellies or boots help on wet grass
Café and bookshop at the car park

places.name: Trim Castle
places.summary: Ireland's largest Anglo-Norman castle, a massive 12th-century keep beside the River Boyne, used as a film location for 'Braveheart'. Climb the keep for views over the town.
facts: Keep by guided tour only (~€5); limited numbers, first come first served
Grounds-only ticket cheaper
Closed some weekdays in winter; check OPW site

places.name: Loughcrew Cairns
places.summary: Hilltop Neolithic passage tombs with carved stones and huge views, far quieter than Newgrange. Cairn T is lit by the sunrise at the spring and autumn equinoxes.
facts: Free; steep 15-minute walk up from the car park
Cairn T has a gate; key/guide arrangement varies, check locally
Wear boots, it's often muddy

places.name: Carlingford
places.summary: Medieval village on Carlingford Lough beneath the Cooley Mountains, with King John's Castle, narrow lanes and oysters. The Mourne Mountains rise across the water.
facts: Free parking by the harbour
Carlingford Greenway runs 7 km along the lough to Omeath
Busy with hen and stag parties at weekends

places.name: Kilkenny
places.summary: Medieval city with a castle, cathedral, the 'Medieval Mile' of lanes and some of Ireland's best traditional pubs. One of the most pleasant towns to stay in the southeast.
facts: Pay car parks around the centre; everything is walkable
Medieval Mile Museum tells the town's story
Kilkenny Design Centre faces the castle

places.name: Kilkenny Castle
places.summary: 12th-century Norman castle remodelled in Victorian times, with restored state rooms, a long picture gallery and big riverside parkland. Seat of the Butler family for 600 years.
facts: Self-guided ~€8; parkland free
Allow 1–1.5 hours
Opposite the Design Centre

places.name: St Canice's Cathedral & Round Tower
places.summary: 13th-century Gothic cathedral with fine tomb effigies and a 9th-century round tower you can climb by internal ladders for views over Kilkenny.
facts: Cathedral ~€7, round tower extra; combined ticket available
Tower climb is steep and not for small children
Tower closes in bad weather

places.name: Jerpoint Abbey
places.summary: Cistercian abbey ruin famous for the carved figures on its cloister arcade: knights, saints and dragons. Among the best-preserved medieval monasteries in Ireland.
facts: Entry ~€5 (OPW)
Seasonal opening; may be closed in deep winter
20 minutes south of Kilkenny

places.name: Dunmore Cave
places.summary: Limestone cave with large chambers and stalagmites, also the site of a Viking massacre in 928. Visited on guided tours down a long staircase.
facts: Guided tour ~€5 (OPW)
Around 350 steps; cool and damp inside
Winter opening reduced to some days

places.name: Inistioge
places.summary: Pretty village with a ten-arch stone bridge over the River Nore, a tree-lined square and walks in Woodstock Gardens above the town.
facts: Woodstock Gardens car park has a small fee
Riverside picnic spot
On the scenic road between Kilkenny and New Ross

places.name: Cashel
places.summary: Market town at the foot of the Rock of Cashel, with good pubs and guesthouses. Handy overnight stop between Dublin and Cork or Kerry.
facts: Free parking in town; Rock car park is paid
Just off the M8 motorway
Evening views of the floodlit Rock

places.name: Rock of Cashel
places.summary: Limestone outcrop crowned by a round tower, a ruined Gothic cathedral and Cormac's Chapel with rare Romanesque frescoes. Seat of the kings of Munster and one of Ireland's iconic sights.
facts: Entry ~€8 (OPW); Cormac's Chapel by guided tour only
Exposed and windy on top; bring a layer
Arrive at opening to beat coach groups

places.name: Hore Abbey
places.summary: Roofless Cistercian abbey in a field below the Rock of Cashel, free and empty compared to its famous neighbour. Great photo angle back to the Rock.
facts: Free, open access across a field
10-minute walk from the Rock
Muddy after rain

places.name: Cahir Castle
places.summary: One of Ireland's largest and best-preserved medieval castles, on a rock island in the River Suir, with intact walls, keep and portcullis.
facts: Entry ~€5 (OPW)
Swiss Cottage, a Regency cottage orné, is a riverside walk away
15 minutes south of Cashel

places.name: Lismore Castle Gardens
places.summary: Spectacular castle above the Blackwater, with seven acres of walled and woodland gardens and contemporary art in the gallery. The castle itself is private.
facts: Gardens ~€15; open spring to autumn only
Lismore town has a heritage centre and cafés
Combine with the Vee drive to Cahir

places.name: Waterford
places.summary: Ireland's oldest city, founded by Vikings in 914, with the compact 'Viking Triangle' of museums, Reginald's Tower and the crystal factory. A lively base for the Copper Coast and the Greenway.
facts: Viking Triangle museums sell a combined ticket
Try a 'blaa', the local soft bread roll
Pay car parks along the quays

places.name: Reginald's Tower & Viking Triangle
places.summary: Ireland's oldest urban civic building, a round stone tower holding Viking treasures, and next to it the Medieval Museum and Bishop's Palace. Together they tell 1,000 years of Waterford history.
facts: Reginald's Tower ~€5 (OPW); other museums ticketed separately or combined
Medieval Museum includes an underground chorister's hall
Allow 2 hours for all three

places.name: House of Waterford Crystal
places.summary: Factory tour where you watch glassblowers and cutters at work, followed by a large showroom. Good for a wet day in Waterford.
facts: Guided tour ~€15–20; book ahead in summer
Tours last about 1 hour
On the Mall, next to the Viking Triangle

places.name: Waterford Greenway
places.summary: 46 km traffic-free cycling and walking trail on an old railway line from Waterford to Dungarvan, over viaducts and through a tunnel near the coast. Bike hire firms run shuttles back.
facts: Bike hire ~€25–35 a day including shuttle
Kilmacthomas viaduct is the halfway point with cafés
Full route takes about 3–4 hours by bike

places.name: Copper Coast Drive
places.summary: UNESCO Global Geopark stretch of coves, sea stacks and old copper mine ruins between Tramore and Dungarvan along the R675. Quieter than the west coast but very scenic.
facts: Free; small car parks at Bunmahon and Kilmurrin coves
Geopark visitor centre at Bunmahon
Allow half a day with stops

places.name: Dungarvan
places.summary: Harbour town at the end of the Waterford Greenway, with a Norman castle, a strong food scene and the Comeragh Mountains behind.
facts: Free parking along the quays
Good stop between Waterford and Cork
Helvick Head and the Ring Gaeltacht are nearby

places.name: Hook Lighthouse
places.summary: One of the oldest operational lighthouses in the world, a medieval tower on the tip of the Hook Peninsula. Guided tours climb the 115 steps for sea views.
facts: Guided tour ~€12–14
Café in the old keepers' houses
Rough seas over the rocks in winter storms are dramatic

places.name: Tintern Abbey (Wexford)
places.summary: Cistercian abbey founded by William Marshal, later converted into a house, set in woodland with walled gardens and lakeside paths.
facts: Grounds free; abbey tours in summer (~€5)
Woodland walks of 1–2 hours
On the way to Hook Head

places.name: Dunbrody Famine Ship (New Ross)
places.summary: Full-scale replica of an 1840s emigrant ship on the New Ross quays, with costumed actors bringing passengers' stories to life. A vivid introduction to the Famine emigration.
facts: Guided tour ~€12–15
Tours run about every hour
Kennedy ancestral homestead is 10 minutes away

places.name: Wexford
places.summary: Viking-founded harbour town with narrow streets, a famous opera festival in October and easy access to the sunny southeast beaches.
facts: Quayside car parks; centre is walkable
Wexford Festival Opera in Oct–Nov fills hotels
Rosslare ferry port is 20 minutes away

places.name: Irish National Heritage Park
places.summary: Open-air park with reconstructions of 9,000 years of Irish life: a Mesolithic camp, crannóg, ringfort, monastery and Viking boatyard, connected by woodland trails.
facts: Entry ~€12–15; guided tours included in season
Allow 2 hours
Good for children

places.name: Johnstown Castle
places.summary: Gothic Revival castle with lakes, woodland gardens and the Irish Agricultural Museum in the grounds. Castle tours include the servants' tunnel.
facts: Combined ticket ~€14 for castle, museum and gardens
Grounds alone are cheaper
10 minutes south of Wexford

places.name: Curracloe Beach
places.summary: Long sandy beach backed by dunes and forest, used to film the D-Day landing in 'Saving Private Ryan'. Great for long walks.
facts: Free parking at several access points
Lifeguards in July–August
Raven Nature Reserve forest trails at the south end

places.name: Cork
places.summary: Ireland's second city on an island in the River Lee, with a strong food culture, independent pubs, the English Market and the Shandon bells. Good base for Blarney, Cobh and Kinsale.
facts: Park-and-ride or multi-storeys; the centre is easy on foot
Climb Shandon tower and ring the bells yourself
Lively student city with great live music

places.name: English Market
places.summary: Covered food market dating from 1788, with fishmongers, butchers selling drisheen and tripe, bakers and cheese stalls. The upstairs café is a classic lunch spot.
facts: Free entry
Closed Sundays and bank holidays
Mornings are best for fresh produce

places.name: Saint Fin Barre's Cathedral
places.summary: Exuberant French Gothic cathedral by William Burges, with three spires, rich mosaics and carvings, on the site of Cork's founding monastery.
facts: Entry ~€7
Allow 30–40 minutes
Short walk south of the centre across the river

places.name: Blarney Castle & Gardens
places.summary: Partly ruined 15th-century tower house where visitors lean backwards over the battlements to kiss the Blarney Stone. The big gardens, including the Poison Garden, are the real draw.
facts: Tickets ~€20; book online to save
Queue for the Stone can exceed an hour in summer; arrive at opening
Steep narrow stairs to the top

places.name: Cobh
places.summary: Colourful harbour town on Great Island, the last port of call of the Titanic and departure point for millions of emigrants. St Colman's Cathedral towers above the 'deck of cards' houses.
facts: Train from Cork takes 25 minutes
Titanic Experience and the Cobh Heritage Centre are both on the waterfront
Ferries to Spike Island leave from the town

places.name: Spike Island
places.summary: Island fortress in Cork Harbour used as a monastery, star fort and prison for 1,300 years, now an excellent museum visited by ferry from Cobh.
facts: Ferry and tour ~€25; book ahead
Allow at least half a day including the crossing
Exposed; bring a waterproof
places.season: Daily sailings in summer, weekends only or reduced in winter.

places.name: Jameson Distillery Midleton
places.summary: Tour of the old Midleton distillery buildings, where Jameson and other Irish whiskeys are made, ending with a tasting.
facts: Tours ~€25+; book ahead
Designated drivers get a takeaway sample
Midleton town has a good Saturday farmers' market

places.name: Fota Wildlife Park
places.summary: Open wildlife park where giraffes, cheetahs and lemurs roam large paddocks, with many animals free to wander. One of the top family days out in Ireland.
facts: Tickets ~€20 adult; online booking cheaper
Fota train station is on the Cork–Cobh line
Fota House and gardens are next door

places.name: Kinsale
places.summary: Colourful harbour town with narrow streets, galleries and some of Ireland's best seafood restaurants. Start of the Wild Atlantic Way.
facts: Parking is tight in summer; use the car parks by the harbour
Walk the Scilly path to Charles Fort (about 45 minutes)
Book restaurants ahead in summer

places.name: Charles Fort
places.summary: Huge 17th-century star-shaped fort guarding Kinsale harbour, garrisoned until 1922. Wonderful views over the harbour mouth.
facts: Entry ~€5 (OPW)
Walk from Kinsale via Scilly or drive
Allow 1–1.5 hours

places.name: Clonakilty
places.summary: Lively market town known for black pudding, trad music and the Michael Collins Centre. A good base for West Cork beaches and stone circles.
facts: Free parking in town car parks
De Barra's pub is a well-known music venue
Inchydoney beach is 5 minutes away

places.name: Inchydoney Beach
places.summary: Two Blue Flag sandy beaches either side of a headland, among the finest in West Cork. Popular for surfing and long walks.
facts: Free parking
Surf school on the beach
Lifeguards in summer; strong currents near the headland
places.caution: Rip currents near the headland; swim between the flags.

places.name: Drombeg Stone Circle
places.summary: Well-preserved Bronze Age circle of 17 stones on a terrace with views to the sea, aligned to the winter solstice sunset. Next to it is an ancient cooking pit (fulacht fiadh).
facts: Free, open access
Small car park, 5-minute walk
Close to Glandore and Union Hall harbours

places.name: Baltimore
places.summary: Harbour village at the end of the road in West Cork, with a castle, a white 'Beacon' on the cliffs and ferries to Sherkin and Cape Clear islands.
facts: The Beacon is a short drive or 20-minute walk from the village
Ferries to Sherkin (10 min) and Cape Clear (45 min)
Whale-watching trips run in summer and autumn

places.name: Lough Hyne
places.summary: Marine lake fed by tidal rapids, Ireland's first marine nature reserve. Walk up Knockomagh Wood for views, or join a night kayak trip to see bioluminescence.
facts: Free; small car park at the lake
Knockomagh Wood climb about 40 minutes return
Night kayaking tours run in summer

places.name: Cape Clear Island
places.summary: Ireland's most southerly inhabited island, an Irish-speaking community with cliff walks, a bird observatory and views of the Fastnet Rock.
facts: Ferry from Baltimore (~45 min); return ~€20
No need for a car; walk the island
Sailings depend on weather
places.caution: Ferries can be cancelled in rough seas; check the day before.

places.name: Mizen Head Signal Station
places.summary: Ireland's most south-westerly point, where a dramatic arched bridge crosses a chasm to the old signal station. Seals, dolphins and occasionally whales in the Atlantic below.
facts: Entry ~€8
About 99 steps down and back up
Very windy; bring a layer

places.name: Bantry House & Garden
places.summary: 18th-century house overlooking Bantry Bay, with Italianate gardens and the 'Hundred Steps' terrace giving superb views over the bay.
facts: Entry ~€15; open spring to autumn
Walk the Hundred Steps for the view
Bantry has a Friday market

places.name: Glengarriff
places.summary: Sheltered village at the head of Bantry Bay with ancient oak woods, seal-watching trips and the boat to Garinish Island. Gateway to the Beara Peninsula.
facts: Glengarriff Woods Nature Reserve has free trails
Boats to Garinish leave from Blue Pool pier
Good overnight stop between West Cork and Kerry

places.name: Garinish Island (Ilnacullin)
places.summary: Island garden created in the 1910s, thriving in the mild Gulf Stream climate, with an Italian garden, Martello tower and views of the mountains. Boats pass a seal colony on the way.
facts: Boat fare (~€15) plus garden entry (~€5)
Boats run about every 30 minutes in season
Closed in winter

places.name: Ring of Beara
places.summary: Rugged, quieter alternative to the Ring of Kerry: a 140 km loop of rocky coast, colourful villages like Eyeries and Allihies, and copper mine ruins.
facts: Allow a full day; roads are narrow and slow
Allihies Copper Mine Museum and beach worth a stop
Few petrol stations; fill up in Glengarriff or Castletownbere

places.name: Healy Pass
places.summary: Spectacular switchback road over the Caha Mountains from Adrigole to Lauragh, with views over Glanmore Lake and both bays.
facts: Free; small viewpoint at the summit
Single-track sections; not for large campervans
Combine with the Ring of Beara
places.caution: Narrow, steep and exposed; avoid in fog or ice.

places.name: Dursey Island Cable Car
places.summary: Ireland's only cable car swings across the sound to Dursey Island at the tip of Beara, with walks to the signal tower and sea cliffs.
facts: Fare ~€10 return; limited cabin size means queues in summer
Island has no shops; bring food and water
Check the cable car schedule as it closes at times for maintenance

places.name: Gougane Barra
places.summary: Mountain lake at the source of the River Lee, with a tiny island oratory of St Finbarr and forest park trails in a glacial valley.
facts: Forest park car park has a small fee
Oratory is free
Narrow roads; 40 minutes from Bantry or Macroom

places.name: Killarney
places.summary: Busy tourist town at the gateway to Killarney National Park, with jaunting cars, lively pubs and lots of accommodation. The natural base for the Ring of Kerry and the Gap of Dunloe.
facts: Large pay car parks; park free in the National Park lots
Book accommodation early for July–August
Train station with direct and connecting services to Dublin and Cork

places.name: Muckross House & Gardens
places.summary: Victorian mansion on the lakeshore in Killarney National Park, visited by Queen Victoria, with gardens, traditional farms and Muckross Abbey nearby.
facts: House tour ~€15; gardens and park free
Rent bikes in Killarney and cycle here
Muckross Abbey ruin is a 15-minute walk

places.name: Ross Castle
places.summary: 15th-century tower house on the shore of Lough Leane, visited by guided tour. Boats leave from here for the lakes and the Gap of Dunloe.
facts: Guided tour ~€5 (OPW), limited numbers
Boat trips on Lough Leane from the pier
Easy cycle or walk from Killarney

places.name: Torc Waterfall
places.summary: 20 m cascade in woodland a short walk from the N71, with steps above for views over the lakes. Can be combined with a climb of Torc Mountain.
facts: Free; small car park often full, use the larger one nearby
5-minute walk to the falls
Best after rain

places.name: Gap of Dunloe
places.summary: Narrow glacial pass between MacGillycuddy's Reeks and the Purple Mountains, walked or cycled from Kate Kearney's Cottage. Classic route: through the Gap, then by boat back across the lakes to Ross Castle.
facts: Road is open to cars but walkers and bikes have priority; don't drive it in summer
Gap + boat combo tickets (~€30–40) can be booked in Killarney
Jaunting cars (horse and trap) also run through the Gap

places.name: Ladies View
places.summary: Celebrated viewpoint on the N71 over the Upper Lake and Killarney valley, named after Queen Victoria's ladies-in-waiting.
facts: Free roadside parking
Café and shop at the viewpoint
On the road from Killarney to Kenmare via Moll's Gap

places.name: Carrauntoohil
places.summary: Ireland's highest mountain (1,039 m) in MacGillycuddy's Reeks, usually climbed from Cronin's Yard via the Hag's Glen. A serious mountain day for fit walkers.
facts: About 6–8 hours return
Small parking fee at Cronin's Yard
Hire a local guide if you lack navigation skills
places.caution: Frequent fog and steep loose ground; people die here most years. Go with a guide unless experienced.

places.name: Kenmare
places.summary: Planned 18th-century town at the head of Kenmare Bay with colourful shops, good restaurants and a stone circle. A quieter base than Killarney, between the Ring of Kerry and Beara.
facts: Free and pay parking around the square
Kenmare stone circle is a short walk (~€2)
Good for food; book dinner ahead in summer

places.name: Ring of Kerry (Coomakesta Pass)
places.summary: 179 km loop around the Iveragh Peninsula with mountains, beaches and islands; the view from Coomakesta Pass over Derrynane and the Skelligs is a highlight. Detour via the Skellig Ring for the wilder scenery.
facts: Allow a full day; drive anticlockwise (Killarney–Killorglin–Cahersiveen) as tour coaches do
Narrow roads; average speed is low
Stops: Kells Bay, Cahersiveen, Waterville, Derrynane, Sneem
places.caution: Tour coaches take up the whole road on bends; be ready to pull in.

places.name: Derrynane Beach & House
places.summary: Sheltered white-sand beaches and dunes on the Ring of Kerry, next to the home of Daniel O'Connell, now a museum in a national historic park.
facts: Park free; Derrynane House ~€5 (OPW)
Walk out to Abbey Island at low tide
Swimming only at the lifeguarded beach in summer
places.caution: Strong currents off parts of the beach; swim only where flagged.

places.name: Portmagee
places.summary: Colourful fishing village facing Valentia Island and the departure point for Skellig Michael boats. Start of the Skellig Ring.
facts: Book accommodation early if you have a Skellig landing trip
Kerry Cliffs (~€5) are 5 minutes away
Pubs with music on summer nights

places.name: Skellig Michael
places.summary: UNESCO-listed 6th-century monastery of beehive huts perched 180 m up on a jagged Atlantic rock, reached by 600 steep steps. Boats leave from Portmagee; also a Star Wars location.
facts: Landing trips run roughly mid-May to September with a few licensed boats; book months ahead
Eco-tours that circle the island without landing are easier to get
Around 5–6 hours including 45–60 minutes each way by boat
places.caution: Steep, unrailed steps and rough crossings; trips are often cancelled in bad weather.
places.season: Landings only in summer, weather permitting; puffins nest until about early August.

places.name: Kerry Cliffs
places.summary: 300 m cliffs on private land near Portmagee with sweeping views to the Skellig islands. A quieter alternative to the Cliffs of Moher.
facts: Entry ~€5 at the gate
Short uphill walk from the car park
Best in clear afternoon light

places.name: Valentia Island
places.summary: Island linked by bridge to Portmagee, with Geokaun Mountain viewpoint, a 385-million-year-old tetrapod trackway and the first transatlantic telegraph station.
facts: Geokaun Mountain road (~€5 per car) for the island's best view
Summer car ferry from Knightstown to Reenard near Cahersiveen
Slate quarry grotto is free

places.name: Dingle
places.summary: Colourful fishing town known for its pubs, music, seafood and ice cream, set on a harbour in the Irish-speaking Gaeltacht. The base for Slea Head and the Dingle Peninsula.
facts: Parking is tight in summer; use the pier car parks
Book accommodation and dinner well ahead in high season
Pubs with trad music most nights

places.name: Slea Head Drive
places.summary: 47 km loop west of Dingle past beehive huts, cliffs, Dunquin harbour and the Blasket Islands, on Europe's westernmost edge. One of the most beautiful drives in Ireland.
facts: Drive clockwise (Ventry first), as road signs advise
Allow half a day with stops
Dún Chaoin and Coumeenoole beach are must-stops
places.caution: Narrow cliff road with low walls; take it slowly.

places.name: Blasket Centre
places.summary: Heritage centre in Dunquin telling the story of the Great Blasket islanders and their extraordinary literature, with views across to the abandoned island.
facts: Entry ~€5 (OPW)
Boats to Great Blasket Island leave from Dunquin pier in summer
Allow an hour

places.name: Gallarus Oratory
places.summary: Early Christian dry-stone oratory shaped like an upturned boat, still watertight after over 1,000 years.
facts: Free via a public path; or a small fee at the visitor centre car park
Combine with Kilmalkedar church nearby
15 minutes from Dingle

places.name: Conor Pass
places.summary: Ireland's highest mountain pass road at about 410 m, with views over corrie lakes to Brandon Bay and Dingle Harbour.
facts: Free parking at the summit viewpoint
Very narrow section north of the summit; no buses or large vehicles
Short scramble to Pedlar's Lake
places.caution: Single-track with steep drops; avoid in fog or with a large campervan.

places.name: Inch Beach
places.summary: Five km sandy spit reaching into Dingle Bay, popular for surfing and long walks, and a filming location for 'Ryan's Daughter'.
facts: Free parking (cars allowed on the beach in parts)
Surf schools in summer
Lifeguards in July–August

places.name: Limerick
places.summary: River Shannon city with a Norman castle, Georgian quarter and the Hunt Museum, plus a strong rugby and food culture. A practical base near Shannon Airport.
facts: Pay parking in multi-storeys; centre is walkable
Milk Market runs Friday to Sunday
Shannon Airport is 25 minutes away

places.name: King John's Castle
places.summary: 13th-century castle on King's Island by the Shannon, with an interactive exhibition, excavated siege tunnels and views from the battlements.
facts: Tickets ~€15; cheaper online
Allow 1.5 hours
St Mary's Cathedral is a 5-minute walk

places.name: Hunt Museum
places.summary: Eclectic private collection of art and antiquities from the Bronze Age to Picasso, in the Georgian Custom House on the river.
facts: Entry ~€10
Riverside café
Good wet-weather option

places.name: Adare
places.summary: Often called Ireland's prettiest village, with thatched cottages, medieval abbeys and a Desmond castle by the River Maigue.
facts: Free car park by the heritage centre
Desmond Castle visited by tour from the heritage centre in summer
Busy with coach tours at midday

places.name: Bunratty Castle & Folk Park
places.summary: Restored 15th-century tower house furnished in period style, with a folk park of recreated rural cottages, shops and a village street. Medieval banquets are held in the evenings.
facts: Tickets ~€15–20; cheaper online
Allow 2–3 hours
10 minutes from Shannon Airport, handy on arrival or departure day

places.name: Ennis
places.summary: Clare's lively county town with narrow streets, a ruined Franciscan friary and a strong trad music scene. Central base for the Burren and the coast.
facts: Pay parking in town car parks
Ennis Friary (OPW) has fine medieval carvings
Trad sessions in pubs most nights

places.name: Quin Abbey
places.summary: Well-preserved Franciscan friary with an intact cloister and tower you can climb, free and often empty.
facts: Free, open access
Allow 30 minutes
Between Ennis and Bunratty

places.name: Doolin
places.summary: Scattered village famous for traditional music, close to the Cliffs of Moher and with ferries to the Aran Islands. Good base for the cliffs and the Burren.
facts: Pubs with music nightly in summer
Ferries to Inis Oírr and Inis Mór from Doolin pier (seasonal)
Book accommodation early in summer

places.name: Cliffs of Moher
places.summary: Sheer sea cliffs rising to 214 m over the Atlantic, stretching 8 km along the Clare coast, with puffins in early summer. Ireland's most visited natural sight.
facts: Admission ~€10–12 includes parking and the visitor centre; cheaper online
Arrive early morning or late afternoon to avoid crowds
Walk south toward Hag's Head for quieter views
places.caution: Stay behind the barriers and on paths; edges are unstable and winds can be extreme.
places.season: Puffins nest from about April to July; winter storms bring huge waves.

places.name: Doolin to Cliffs of Moher Coastal Walk
places.summary: Clifftop path from Doolin to the Cliffs of Moher visitor centre, the most dramatic way to see the cliffs. The Doolin end now runs as guided walks.
facts: About 8 km one way, 2.5–3 hours
Access from the Doolin end is by local guided walk; check locally
Arrange a taxi or bus back
places.caution: Unfenced cliff edges; not in high wind or poor visibility.

places.name: Doolin Cave
places.summary: Cave holding the Great Stalactite, one of the longest free-hanging stalactites in the world at over 7 m, seen on a guided tour.
facts: Guided tour ~€17; book ahead in summer
Farm nature trail included
Tour lasts about an hour

places.name: Aillwee Cave
places.summary: Show cave in the Burren with an underground river, waterfall and bear bones, plus a birds of prey centre.
facts: Tickets ~€15; birds of prey extra or combined
Guided tours about 35 minutes
Near Ballyvaughan

places.name: Poulnabrone Dolmen
places.summary: Neolithic portal tomb over 5,000 years old, standing on the bare limestone pavement of the Burren. Iconic photo spot.
facts: Free; car park by the road
Stay on the path; the pavement is fragile
Best in low light early or late

places.name: Burren National Park (Mullaghmore)
places.summary: Strange limestone landscape of terraced hills, pavements and rare alpine and Mediterranean flowers. Waymarked loops climb Mullaghmore.
facts: Free; small car parks at the trailheads
Information point in Corofin in summer
Mullaghmore loop takes about 3 hours
places.season: Wildflowers peak in May and June.

places.name: Fanore & the Coast Road
places.summary: Dune-backed beach on the Burren coast road from Ballyvaughan to Doolin, with limestone terraces dropping to the sea at Black Head.
facts: Free parking
Surf school in summer
Coast road R477 is very scenic

places.name: Lahinch
places.summary: Surf town with a long sandy beach and a famous links golf course, 15 minutes south of the Cliffs of Moher.
facts: Several surf schools; wetsuit hire available
Pay parking on the promenade
Lively in summer

places.name: Kilkee
places.summary: Victorian seaside resort on a horseshoe bay, with a spectacular cliff walk west of the town.
facts: Kilkee Cliff Walk loop is about 8 km
Pollock Holes rock pools for swimming at low tide
Gateway to Loop Head

places.name: Loop Head Lighthouse
places.summary: Lighthouse at the tip of the Loop Head peninsula, where the Shannon meets the Atlantic, with sea stacks, dolphins and wild cliffs.
facts: Lighthouse tour ~€6 in season; headland free
Look for the Bridges of Ross natural arch on the way
Dolphin trips from Carrigaholt in summer

places.name: Killaloe & Ballina
places.summary: Twin villages linked by a 13-arch bridge at the south end of Lough Derg, with a cathedral, lakeside walks and boat trips.
facts: Lough Derg cruises run in summer
Free parking on both sides of the bridge
Lough Derg Way and lakeside drives nearby

places.name: Galway
places.summary: Lively bohemian city with street musicians, colourful shopfronts in the Latin Quarter, oysters and many trad pubs. The base for Connemara, the Burren and the Aran Islands.
facts: Driving in the centre is slow; use the park-and-ride or multi-storeys
Shop Street, Quay Street and the Spanish Arch are all within 10 minutes' walk
Galway International Arts Festival (July) and Races (August) fill hotels

places.name: Galway Cathedral
places.summary: One of the last great stone cathedrals built in Europe, completed in 1965, with a green copper dome and striking mosaics.
facts: Free; donations welcome
Across the Salmon Weir Bridge from the old town
Open daily except during services

places.name: Salthill Promenade
places.summary: Two-km seafront walk overlooking Galway Bay toward the Burren hills, where locals 'kick the wall' at the end. Blackrock diving tower is popular year-round.
facts: Free; pay parking along the prom
Lovely at sunset
20-minute walk from the city centre

places.name: Dunguaire Castle
places.summary: Picturesque 16th-century tower house on a rocky outcrop by Kinvara harbour, one of the most photographed castles in Ireland.
facts: Interior visits seasonal (~€8); exterior free
Medieval banquets in summer evenings
Kinvara village is a pleasant stop

places.name: Aughnanure Castle
places.summary: Six-storey tower house of the O'Flaherty clan by a river near Oughterard, on the road into Connemara.
facts: Entry ~€5 (OPW); seasonal opening
Allow 45 minutes
Oughterard village has cafés

places.name: Clifden
places.summary: Capital of Connemara, a small Victorian town under the Twelve Bens with good pubs and seafood. Base for the Sky Road and Connemara National Park.
facts: Free parking in town car parks
Book dinner ahead in summer
Alcock and Brown landing site and Derrigimlagh bog nearby

places.name: Sky Road
places.summary: Sixteen-km loop west of Clifden climbing high above Clifden Bay, with views of islands and the Atlantic from the upper road.
facts: Free; viewpoint car park on the upper road
Narrow road; take care with oncoming traffic
Also good by bike

places.name: Roundstone
places.summary: Fishing village on a harbour below Errisbeg hill, with craft shops and seafood. Close to the white beaches at Dog's Bay and Gurteen.
facts: Climb Errisbeg (about 2 hours return) for wide views
Coast road to Ballyconneely and Clifden is lovely
Small, quiet place to stay

places.name: Dog's Bay & Gurteen Beaches
places.summary: Twin white shell-sand beaches back to back on a tombolo, with turquoise water that looks Caribbean on sunny days.
facts: Small car park, often full in summer
Water is cold year-round
Short walk across the dunes between the two beaches

places.name: Connemara National Park & Diamond Hill
places.summary: Bog, heath and mountains in the heart of Connemara, with a well-built path up Diamond Hill giving views over Kylemore and the coast. Connemara ponies graze near the visitor centre.
facts: Free entry and parking at Letterfrack
Upper Diamond Hill loop is about 7 km, 2.5–3 hours
Shorter lower loops for an easy walk
places.caution: Summit is exposed and can be very windy; turn back in bad weather.

places.name: Kylemore Abbey & Victorian Walled Garden
places.summary: Neo-Gothic castle reflected in a lake below the mountains, home to Benedictine nuns since 1920. A shuttle runs to a restored six-acre Victorian walled garden.
facts: Tickets roughly €15–20; online booking advised in summer
Allow 2–3 hours including the garden
Gothic church on the lakeside walk

places.name: Inagh Valley
places.summary: Quiet valley road between the Twelve Bens and the Maumturk Mountains, along Lough Inagh and Derryclare Lough. One of Connemara's finest drives.
facts: Free; few stopping places, use the lay-bys
Connects Recess to Kylemore
Watch for sheep on the road

places.name: Killary Harbour & Leenaun
places.summary: Long, deep fjord-like inlet marking the Galway–Mayo border, with mussel rafts and mountains on both sides. Leenaun village sits at its head.
facts: Boat cruises on the fjord run in summer
Aasleagh Falls is 5 minutes east of Leenaun
Famine Walk on the north shore is quiet

places.name: Inis Mór (Kilronan)
places.summary: Largest of the Aran Islands, a world of stone walls, cliffs and Irish-speaking villages. Ferries land at Kilronan, where you can hire bikes or take a minibus tour.
facts: Bike hire ~€15 a day at the pier
Stay overnight to see the island after the day-trippers leave
Cars are not taken by visitors
places.caution: Ferries can be cancelled in rough weather; leave slack in your plans.

places.name: Dún Aonghasa
places.summary: Prehistoric stone fort on the edge of 100 m sea cliffs on Inis Mór, surrounded by a field of stone spikes. One of Europe's most dramatic archaeological sites.
facts: Entry ~€5 (OPW); 20-minute uphill walk from the visitor centre
No railings at the cliff edge
About 7 km from Kilronan by bike or minibus
places.caution: The cliff edge is sheer and unprotected; keep well back, especially in wind.

places.name: Inis Oírr
places.summary: Smallest Aran Island, close to Doolin, with a ruined O'Brien castle, a sand-buried church and the rusting Plassy shipwreck. Easy to walk in a few hours.
facts: Ferry from Doolin (~30 min) in season
Walk or hire a bike at the pier
Pony and trap tours available

places.name: Westport
places.summary: Georgian planned town on the Carrowbeg River with tree-lined streets, lively pubs and Westport House. The base for Croagh Patrick, Achill and the Greenway.
facts: Free and pay car parks in the centre
Matt Molloy's pub has trad music most nights
Book ahead in summer

places.name: Croagh Patrick
places.summary: Ireland's holy mountain (764 m), climbed by pilgrims since St Patrick fasted on its summit. Stunning views over the islands of Clew Bay from the top.
facts: About 3.5–4 hours return from the Murrisk car park (paid)
Upper section is loose scree; good boots and poles help
Reek Sunday pilgrimage (late July) is extremely busy
places.caution: Loose scree causes many injuries on the descent; don't climb in fog or high wind.

places.name: Great Western Greenway
places.summary: 42 km off-road cycle trail on an old railway from Westport via Newport to Achill, with views over Clew Bay. Bike hire firms offer shuttles back.
facts: Bike hire ~€25–35 a day, e-bikes available
Newport to Mulranny is the most scenic section
Allow 3–4 hours for the full route

places.name: Achill Island
places.summary: Ireland's largest island, joined to the mainland by bridge, with Atlantic Drive, high cliffs, a deserted village and some of the best beaches in the country.
facts: Atlantic Drive loop from Achill Sound takes 1–2 hours
Deserted Village at Slievemore is free
Keel and Dugort make good bases

places.name: Keem Bay
places.summary: Sheltered horseshoe beach of white sand and turquoise water at the western tip of Achill, reached by a cliff road. Often listed among Ireland's most beautiful beaches.
facts: Free parking at the beach, fills on sunny days
Walk up to the cliffs above for the classic view
Lifeguard in July and August
places.caution: Cliff road down is narrow; the hills above have sheer drops to the sea.

places.name: Céide Fields
places.summary: World's most extensive Neolithic field system, preserved for 5,000 years beneath blanket bog, with a pyramid-shaped visitor centre above 110 m sea cliffs.
facts: Entry ~€5 (OPW); guided tours of the bog
Open seasonally; check before going
Remote: combine with Downpatrick Head

places.name: Downpatrick Head
places.summary: Headland with the spectacular sea stack Dún Briste, separated from the cliffs by a chasm, and blowholes in the grass.
facts: Free; car park and 10-minute walk
Fenced viewing area at the edge
Puffins and seabirds in summer
places.caution: The blowhole and cliff edges are dangerous; stay on the path.

places.name: National Museum of Ireland – Country Life
places.wiki: National Museum of Ireland – Country Life
places.summary: Free national museum at Turlough Park near Castlebar on Irish rural life from 1850 to 1950: crafts, farming, fishing and folk customs, with a Victorian house and gardens.
facts: Free entry
Allow 1.5–2 hours
Opens later on Sundays and Mondays

places.name: Cong & Ashford Castle
places.summary: Village between Lough Corrib and Lough Mask, with a ruined Augustinian abbey and the grounds of Ashford Castle hotel. Film location of 'The Quiet Man'.
facts: Cong Abbey and woods are free
Ashford Castle grounds charge an entry fee for non-guests
Lough Corrib boat trips in summer

places.name: Sligo
places.summary: Lively riverside town in 'Yeats Country', with an abbey, the Model arts centre and good food, surrounded by mountains, megaliths and surf beaches.
facts: Pay parking around the centre
Sligo Abbey (OPW) has fine carvings
Trad music in pubs most nights

places.name: Carrowmore Megalithic Cemetery
places.summary: One of Ireland's largest collections of Stone Age tombs, around 30 dolmens and stone circles in fields beneath Knocknarea.
facts: Entry ~€5 (OPW); seasonal visitor centre
Allow 1 hour
Combine with the Knocknarea climb

places.name: Knocknarea
places.summary: Flat-topped hill crowned by the huge cairn said to be Queen Maeve's grave, with wide views over Sligo Bay. A short, steep path from the car park.
facts: About 1.5 hours return from the Queen Maeve trail car park
Don't climb on the cairn
Windy on top

places.name: Strandhill
places.summary: Surf village with an Atlantic beach under Knocknarea, known for seaweed baths and lively cafés.
facts: Seaweed baths at the seafront
Surf schools on the beach
Swimming is dangerous here; strong currents
places.caution: Swimming off the main beach is unsafe due to rip currents.

places.name: Drumcliffe & Yeats Grave
places.summary: Churchyard where W.B. Yeats is buried 'under bare Ben Bulben's head', with a high cross and round tower stump from an early monastery.
facts: Free; small café by the church
Allow 30–40 minutes
Benbulben views from the car park

places.name: Benbulben (Gortarowey Walk)
places.summary: Dramatic flat-topped table mountain, a landmark of Sligo. The easy Gortarowey forest loop gives close-up views of its fluted cliffs.
facts: Free; Gortarowey loop about 1 hour
Summit routes cross private land; follow local guidance
Best seen in late afternoon light

places.name: Glencar Waterfall
places.summary: Woodland waterfall above Glencar Lough that inspired Yeats' poem 'The Stolen Child'. The valley road is lined with streams pouring off the cliffs.
facts: Small car park (fee)
Short easy path
Best after rain

places.name: Mullaghmore
places.summary: Fishing village on a headland with a sandy beach and Classiebawn Castle, known for giant winter surf waves.
facts: Headland loop drive or walk with Atlantic views
Beach is good for families
Big-wave surfing in winter storms

places.name: Donegal Town
places.summary: Small market town around a triangular 'Diamond' at the mouth of the River Eske, with a restored O'Donnell castle. Gateway to south-west Donegal.
facts: Free parking at the pier
Water bus tours of Donegal Bay in summer
Good base for Slieve League

places.name: Donegal Castle
places.summary: 15th-century O'Donnell tower house with a Jacobean manor added in the 1600s, beautifully restored with period furnishings.
facts: Entry ~€5 (OPW)
Allow 45 minutes
In the town centre

places.name: Slieve League Cliffs
places.summary: Among the highest sea cliffs in Europe at around 600 m, falling in coloured bands to the Atlantic. The Bunglass viewpoint is the classic view; walkers continue along One Man's Pass.
facts: Free; park at the lower car park and walk or shuttle up, or drive to the upper lot when allowed
Visitor centre at Teelin
Allow 2 hours with a walk
places.caution: One Man's Pass is narrow and exposed; only in good weather with experience.

places.name: Glencolmcille
places.summary: Remote Irish-speaking valley at the western end of Donegal, with a folk village museum, standing stones and wild coastal walks.
facts: Folk Village museum ~€6, seasonal
Glen Head loop walk is spectacular
Very limited services; fill up on fuel

places.name: Glenveagh National Park & Castle
places.summary: Ireland's second-largest national park, a wild valley of mountains, lakes and red deer, with a Victorian castle and gardens on the shore of Lough Veagh.
facts: Park free; shuttle bus to the castle ~€3, castle tour ~€7
Cars are not allowed beyond the visitor centre
Walk or cycle the 4 km lakeside road

places.name: Errigal
places.summary: Donegal's highest peak (751 m), a pink quartzite cone visible from far away. The standard route from the R251 car park takes about 3 hours return.
facts: Free; small car park on the R251
Steep scree near the top; boots needed
Poisoned Glen views from Dunlewey nearby
places.caution: Frequent cloud on the summit; navigation needed in poor visibility.

places.name: Dunfanaghy
places.summary: Small resort village on Sheephaven Bay near Horn Head and the beaches of Killahoey and Marble Hill. A good base for north Donegal.
facts: Workhouse heritage centre in the village
Killahoey beach is walkable from the village
Book ahead in summer

places.name: Horn Head
places.summary: Peninsula of quartzite cliffs rising to 180 m, with a loop road and views across to Tory Island and Errigal.
facts: Free; parking at the old signal tower
Narrow loop road from Dunfanaghy
Seabird colonies in summer
places.caution: High unfenced cliffs; keep away from the edge in wind.

places.name: Fanad Head Lighthouse
places.summary: Lighthouse on a dramatic headland between Lough Swilly and Mulroy Bay, often rated one of the most beautiful in the world. Tours climb the tower.
facts: Tower tour ~€10
You can stay in the keepers' cottages
About an hour from Letterkenny

places.name: Malin Head
places.summary: Ireland's most northerly point at the tip of the Inishowen Peninsula, with a signal tower, 'EIRE' WWII sign in stones and wild seas. A Star Wars filming location.
facts: Free parking at Banba's Crown
Chance of the Northern Lights on clear winter nights
Allow time for the Inishowen 100 drive

places.name: Grianán of Aileach
places.summary: Restored stone ringfort on a hilltop near Derry, seat of the Northern Uí Néill kings, with 360-degree views over Lough Swilly and Lough Foyle.
facts: Free, open access
Short uphill walk from the car park
Very windy on top

places.name: Athlone
places.summary: Bustling river town on the Shannon at the centre of Ireland, with a castle, riverside bars and boat trips to Clonmacnoise. Sean's Bar claims to be Ireland's oldest pub.
facts: Pay parking around the centre
Boat cruises to Clonmacnoise and Lough Ree in summer
On the Dublin–Galway rail line

places.name: Athlone Castle
places.summary: Norman castle by the Shannon with an interactive exhibition on the 1691 Siege of Athlone.
facts: Entry ~€10
Allow 1 hour
Riverside, by the bridge

places.name: Clonmacnoise
places.summary: Early Christian monastery founded in 544 on the banks of the Shannon, with ruined churches, round towers and original high crosses in the visitor centre. One of Ireland's most important monastic sites.
facts: Entry ~€8 (OPW)
Original crosses are indoors; replicas stand outside
Arrive early to beat coach tours

places.name: Birr
places.summary: Elegant Georgian town with broad malls and terraces, at the gates of Birr Castle Demesne.
facts: Free parking in town
Good base for Slieve Bloom
Birr Vintage Week in August

places.name: Birr Castle Demesne
places.summary: Gardens and parkland of the Parsons family, home to the 'Leviathan', the world's largest telescope for 70 years, plus Ireland's Historic Science Centre and the tallest box hedges in the world.
facts: Entry ~€12; castle interior by summer tour only
Allow 2–3 hours
Treehouse adventure area for children

places.name: Slieve Bloom Mountains
places.summary: Gentle, quiet range of bog and forest with waymarked loops, waterfalls and the Glenbarrow trail.
facts: Free trails and car parks
Glenbarrow waterfall loop is about 2 hours
Very few visitors outside weekends

places.name: Kilbeggan Distillery
places.summary: One of the oldest licensed distilleries in the world (1757), with a working waterwheel and old machinery on the River Brosna.
facts: Tours ~€15–20 with tasting
Allow about an hour
Just off the M6

places.name: Tullamore D.E.W. Visitor Centre
places.summary: Whiskey heritage centre in an 1897 canal-side bonded warehouse, with tastings and blending experiences.
facts: Tours ~€20 with tasting
Grand Canal towpath next door
Allow about an hour

places.name: Belvedere House & Gardens
places.summary: 18th-century hunting lodge on Lough Ennell, with the 'Jealous Wall', Ireland's largest folly, walled gardens and lakeside woods.
facts: Entry ~€10
Allow 2 hours
Near Mullingar

places.name: Fore Abbey
places.summary: Benedictine priory ruins in a quiet valley, linked to the legendary 'Seven Wonders of Fore' such as water that flows uphill.
facts: Free, open access
Allow 45 minutes
Coffee shop and info in the village

places.name: Strokestown Park & National Famine Museum
places.summary: Palladian mansion with the National Famine Museum, built around the estate's own records of evictions and emigration. A sobering and essential visit.

Allow 2 hours
Walled gardens included

places.name: Rathcroghan (Cruachan Aí)

facts: Visitor centre ~€8; guided cave tours by booking

Allow 1.5 hours

places.name: Carrick-on-Shannon
places.summary: Lively riverside town and boating centre on the upper Shannon, with the tiny Costello Chapel and a busy marina.
facts: Cruiser hire base for Shannon boating holidays
Riverside boardwalk
Lively at weekends

places.name: Portumna Castle
places.summary: Early 17th-century semi-fortified house on the northern shore of Lough Derg, with formal gardens and a forest park.

Portumna Forest Park has lakeside trails
Allow an hour

places.name: Rock of Dunamase
places.summary: Ruins of a Norman castle on a rocky outcrop with sweeping views over the plains of Laois.
facts: Free, open access
Short steep walk from the car park
Just off the M7 near Portlaoise

places.name: Belfast
places.summary: Northern Ireland's capital, transformed in recent decades, with Victorian landmarks, the Titanic Quarter, a thriving pub and food scene and moving political murals.

Black taxi mural tours ~£15–20 per person
City Hall free tours run daily

places.name: Titanic Belfast
places.summary: Striking museum on the slipways where the Titanic was built, telling the story of the ship and of industrial Belfast. Includes the SS Nomadic tender.
facts: Tickets ~£25; timed entry, book online
Allow 2–3 hours
20-minute walk or short bus from the centre

places.name: Ulster Museum

Usually closed on Mondays outside holidays
Botanic Gardens and Palm House are free

places.name: Falls & Shankill Murals

Sign the peace wall like generations of visitors
Walking tours also available

places.name: St George's Market

facts: Free entry; open Friday to Sunday only
Saturday is the busiest for food stalls
Bring cash for some stalls

places.name: Cave Hill
places.summary: Hill above north Belfast whose profile, 'Napoleon's Nose', inspired Gulliver's Travels. A loop walk passes caves and gives views over the city and Belfast Lough.

Loop about 2–3 hours
Muddy after rain

places.name: Carrickfergus Castle
places.summary: One of the best-preserved Norman castles in Ireland, built in 1177 on the shore of Belfast Lough.
facts: Entry ~£7
Allow an hour
Train from Belfast takes about 25 minutes

places.name: The Gobbins Cliff Path
places.summary: Guided walk along a dramatic Edwardian cliff path of bridges and tunnels hugging the basalt cliffs of Islandmagee, just above the waves.

Tours often cancelled in rough seas

places.name: Mount Stewart
places.summary: National Trust house on Strangford Lough with one of Europe's great gardens, full of subtropical plants and quirky topiary.
facts: Entry ~£15 (free for National Trust members)
Allow 2–3 hours
Café on site

places.name: Newcastle
places.summary: Seaside town 'where the Mountains of Mourne sweep down to the sea', with a long beach and promenade. The base for climbing Slieve Donard.
facts: Pay parking on the promenade
Royal County Down golf course is here
Tollymore and Castlewellan forest parks nearby

places.name: Slieve Donard
places.summary: Northern Ireland's highest mountain (850 m), climbed from Newcastle via the Glen River path past the Mourne Wall, with views to Scotland and the Isle of Man on clear days.

Steep, eroded path in the upper section
Start early in summer

places.name: Tollymore Forest Park

Rivers trail loop about 1.5 hours

places.name: Glenariff Forest Park

Waterfall walkway loop about 1 hour

places.name: Causeway Coastal Route & Torr Head

Allow a full day from Belfast to Portrush with stops

places.name: Rathlin Island
places.summary: L-shaped island off Ballycastle with the RSPB West Light Seabird Centre, home to thousands of puffins, guillemots and razorbills in summer.

Shuttle bus or bike hire on the island
Seabird centre open in spring and summer

places.name: Carrick-a-Rede Rope Bridge
places.summary: Rope bridge strung 30 m above the sea to a tiny island once used by salmon fishermen, at the end of a clifftop path.

Closes in high winds

places.name: Ballintoy Harbour
places.summary: Tiny harbour reached by a steep lane, with limestone rocks and sea stacks, used as the Iron Islands in Game of Thrones.

Steep narrow access road
Café in summer

places.name: The Dark Hedges

places.name: Giant's Causeway
places.summary: Around 40,000 interlocking basalt columns stepping into the sea, formed by volcanic activity 60 million years ago. Northern Ireland's only UNESCO World Heritage Site.

places.name: Old Bushmills Distillery

3 km from the Giant's Causeway

places.name: Dunluce Castle

places.name: Portrush

places.name: Whiterocks Beach

Surf schools in summer
Walk along the beach to Dunluce Castle views

places.name: Mussenden Temple & Downhill Demesne
places.summary: Small domed 18th-century temple on a cliff edge above Downhill Strand, with the ruined Downhill House behind. One of Northern Ireland's most photographed sights.

places.name: Derry / Londonderry
places.summary: Only city in Ireland with complete 17th-century walls, with the Bogside murals, the Peace Bridge and a vibrant cultural scene.

places.name: Derry City Walls
places.summary: Intact 17th-century walls encircling the old city, with cannons, gates and views down over the Bogside murals.

Guided walking tours available

Car rental in the car rental centre (shuttle bus)

checklist: Passport or EU ID card. Northern Ireland is in the UK: check whether you need the UK ETA if you cross the border (non-Irish, non-UK citizens).
Driving licence and a credit card for the rental deposit. Tell the rental company if you'll drive into Northern Ireland (cross-border fee).
Drive on the LEFT. Narrow country roads: give way at passing places, watch for sheep, cyclists and tractors.
Rain jacket and layers all year: the weather changes several times a day.
Book timed tickets ahead: the Book of Kells, the Guinness Storehouse, Brú na Bóinne (Newgrange), and Skellig Michael landing tours months ahead.
Many castles, houses and visitor centres close or shorten hours from November to March.
Cliffs (Moher, Slieve League, the Causeway coast): stay behind barriers and away from crumbling edges, especially in wind.
The Atlantic is cold and has rip currents: swim only at lifeguarded beaches in summer.
Plugs are the UK three-pin type (G).
European Health Insurance Card (EU) or travel insurance.
